title: "Choose a Simulation"
description: "Choose a calculation by the electrical quantity you need."

---

Choose the question first, then open a tutorial with the matching geometry,
excitation, and backend. Layout use is independent of solver installation.

| Question | Guide | Starting model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What capacitance does this conductor arrangement have? | [Capacitance](simulation/requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd) | Square pad and surrounding ground |
| What are the natural or loaded modes? | [Resonance & Eigenmodes](simulation/requirements/eigenmode.qmd) | Finite CPW, pad LC, or loaded meander |
| How do signals reflect and transmit? | [S-parameters & Ports](simulation/requirements/driven-terminal.qmd) | CPW–resonator with Lumped or Wave excitation |
| What are the uniform-line parameters? | [Cross-section Simulation](simulation/requirements/q2d-cross-section.qmd) | Explicit Q2D section |
| Where is field energy stored, and how do interface assumptions affect loss? | [Participation & Surface Loss](simulation/requirements/epr-loss.qmd) | Pad LC and local interface regions |

Open a guide above for tutorials and downloads, or browse the
[Model Gallery](public-pdk-examples/test-components.md) for source layouts.

## Before you run

Read the selected tutorial's setup and use its stated OrcaPen, SCGSim, and
solver versions. Optional AEDT and Palace runtimes are separate.
The repository's ordinary dependency groups may differ from a tutorial's required environment.

Keep the tutorial's conductor references, stack, materials, exterior, and port
conventions together. Use a new output directory for a new run; use its
returned-run analysis action to read an existing result.

⚠️ Saved outputs can use earlier model or runtime versions. Check the selected
tutorial's status before treating its displayed results as results of its current source.
